requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
I judge that the reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.authoring.invocation`.

The obligations below are each mapped to a test and its assertions.

- **Authoring one existing subject, requirement or named example.**
  - `fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` runs `habeas author` for both a requirement (`SUBJECT`) and an example (`requirements.ready_case`). It checks that the evidence record is written under `evidence/<subject>.json` with the right `requirement` or `example` field.
  - `fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` shows that a nonexistent subject (`requirements.absent`) fails and names the subject in stderr. It also shows that a subject combined with `--all` is rejected with exit code 2.

- **Completion report content.**
  - The report must name the subject, backend, model, evidence destination and usage-record path.
  - `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` and the example/requirement loop in `fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` assert that stdout starts with `<subject>: ollama / <MODEL>`. They also assert an `Evidence:` line and a `Usage:` line.
  - The usage path is checked to be an existing file.

- **Evidence destination by default.** The `Evidence:` path is asserted to end in `evidence/<SUBJECT>.json` and to resolve to the project's evidence file.

- **`--stdout` mode.**
  - `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` covers true, false and FIXME determinations, with and without existing evidence, and with and without verbose.
  - Stdout parses as pure JSON, so no report or diagnostic text leaks onto it.
  - Stderr contains `<SUBJECT>: ollama / <MODEL>`, `Evidence: stdout`, and a `Usage:` path that is an existing file.
  - Project evidence files are unchanged.

- **Options.**
  - `--config <name>`: `fn[an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile]` selects a non-default profile and asserts the request model, key, and usage backend and model.
  - `--missing` and `--force`: `fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` covers both flags, including their mutual exclusion and `--stdout` implying `--force`. The refresh behavior itself belongs to `requirements.authoring.refresh`.
  - `-v` and `--verbose`: `fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` and the stdout test exercise both spellings.

- **`author-evidence` alias.** Alias use is exercised in `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]`, the stdout test, and `fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]`. The last of these also checks the alias's skipped-as-current output.

I found no scenario the requirement text names that the reviewed tests would accept in violating form.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
